title: Review: def, call, and parameters together
idea: TOOL + review: combine define/call (u71) with parameters, and recall earlier tools. ~30% review.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: what does defining (not calling) a sub-plan do?
options: Sets up its steps but runs nothing yet
exercises.explanation: Defining sets up the steps; calling runs them. Parameters don't change this — they just add slots to fill at call time.

options: A call like greet("Sam"), not shown yet
exercises.explanation: The print only runs when greet is called with a value. Defining greet, even with a parameter, prints nothing.

exercises.prompt: A parameter is a slot named in the def; an argument is the value passed in the call.
exercises.explanation: Yes — the key pair. The argument fills the parameter slot each time you call.
n is 2, so range(2) loops twice, printing x each time. The parameter controls the loop count.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece to its role.

pairs.right: Defines a sub-plan with two parameters

exercises.explanation: Header names the slots, the call fills them, the body uses them. That's the whole shape of a parameterized sub-plan.

exercises.prompt:
def add(a, b):
    print(a + b)

add(10, 5)

What prints?
exercises.explanation: a is 10, b is 5, so 10 + 5 is 15. Two parameters filled in order by the two arguments.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: what does str(12) give, as you'd use it inside a sub-plan?
exercises.explanation: str turns the number 12 into the text "12" so it can join a message. You use it when printing numbers next to words.

exercises.prompt: One parameterized sub-plan can replace many nearly-identical fixed sub-plans.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Instead of greetSam, greetMia, greetLee, you write greet(name) once and pass the name. Parameters crush repetition.

exercises.prompt: Assemble a program: define show_bigger(a, b) that prints the larger, then call it with 3 and 8.
exercises.explanation: The if/else compares the two parameters and prints the larger. show_bigger(3, 8) prints 8 — a decision driven by parameters.

options: Define sub-plans that receive one or more values and print results using them
Only define sub-plans with no values
exercises.explanation: Define, call, and pass values — one or several. Your sub-plans now adapt to whatever the main plan hands them.
